subject: Novus AI — commit tenor, SKU breakpoint & discount escalation
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa@novus.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novus.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft commit proposal and question on SKU breakpoints

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the draft reserved capacity proposal — attached is our version with the volumes we expect across Q4–Q6 (novus_commit_request_v1.pdf). We're broadly comfortable with the nominal commit, but two points came up in procurement and engineering:

1) GPU price volatility: Novus wants clarity on what happens if market GPU prices spike >25% vs. the committed base. Do you have a standard "breakpoint" or indexation approach?
2) Tenor flexibility: If we lock a 24-month commit, what levers exist for mid-term rebalancing (SKU swaps, partial decommit) without triggering full clawbacks?

Procurement asked for sample contract language for a limited-price-escape or indexation clause so they can evaluate with counsel. Can Redwood propose a structure (preferred: a tiered discount schedule with an explicit price-index trigger and a cap on carve-outs)?

Also happy to jump on a short call this week — available Tue/Wed morning PT.

Appreciate it,

Alyssa Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Novus AI
alyssa@novus.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: novus_commit_request_v1.pdf (proposal summary, 3 pages)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@novus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft commit proposal and question on SKU breakpoints

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Looping in Karthik (pricing/strategy) and Ben (finance/discount approvals) so we can validate scenarios and proposed contract language.

Quick notes:
- We can do a tiered discount schedule tied to committed GPU-hours + SKU mix.
- For price spikes, we typically offer an indexation clause (3% floor / 30% cap) or a one-time top-up credit instead of full decommit.
- Tenor rebalancing is doable with phased SKU swaps and a small rebalancing fee; full decommit triggers need exec sign-off above certain $ thresholds.

Karthik — can you run a sensitivity with two scenarios: (A) 24-month commit with indexation trigger at +20% GPU cost, (B) 24-month commit with a hard breakpoint at +30% where limited partial decommiting is allowed (up to 15% of committed capacity) and show P&L impact to Redwood for both? See my rough asks inline in the attached price_sensitivity_model.csv.

Alyssa — once internal alignment is done we'll propose specific legal wording (short redlines) and a preferred option so your counsel can review.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 510-555-0248

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa@novus.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft commit proposal and question on SKU breakpoints — sensitivity scenarios

Folks — ran two high-level sensitivity scenarios against our cost model (see inline summary; full table in price_sensitivity_model.csv). Numbers are conservative and assume current public spot-curve movement patterns + 20% ops overhead for SKU swaps.

Summary (24-month commit, baseline = committed blended unit price):
A) Indexation trigger at +20% GPU cost:
   - Redwood impact: 60–70bps margin compression over 24 months (we'd absorb partial cost up to the 20% level; beyond that we'd pass through pre-agreed incremental surcharge or credit).
   - Customer impact: minimal short-term uplift if surcharge applies; preserves continuity.

B) Hard breakpoint at +30% with partial decommit allowance (up to 15% of committed capacity):
   - Redwood impact: 120–150bps margin compression if break invoked + cost to reallocate parked capacity. Potential for stranded fixed-cost exposure if we can't reassign hardware quickly.
   - Customer impact: stronger downside protection; higher administrative overhead and likely a slightly higher baseline price to compensate.

My recommendation: offer Option A as default (indexation + capped surcharge) and Option B as an escalated negotiated choice for larger deals, but require a price-protection fee (one-time small premium) to opt into Option B.

Questions for Ben: what approval level do we need for a one-time price-protection fee < 2.5% ARR versus a baseline discount swing? If Ben signs off for <$X threshold we can enable Option B for deals under that threshold without exec escalation.

Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@novus.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft commit proposal and question on SKU breakpoints — proposed commercial construct

Hi all — appreciate the patient back-and-forth. Based on Karthik's scenarios, finance is comfortable with a two-track commercial construct:

1) Standard: Indexation clause tied to a GPU cost index (quarterly lookback). If GPU cost increases between 10–25%, Redwood will apply a pre-agreed surcharge tier (0.5%–2.0% of committed spend) rather than altering the committed volumes. This preserves price transparency and continuity.

2) Breakpoint option (negotiable for large deals): Hard breakpoint at +30% GPU cost. If invoked, Novus can elect to decommit up to 15% of committed capacity once during the tenor. Decommit will require a one-time price-protection fee equal to 1.5% of the committed ARR and a 60-day notice window.

Legal & ops notes: we'll propose short redlines to implement the above; the breakpoint option requires head-of-sales approval for deals > $3M ARR. For deals <$3M the finance team can approve the breakpoint option if the price-protection fee is accepted.

Next steps:
- Stephanie: propose preferred option and share with Novus counsel.
- Karthik: finalize the sensitivity CSV and include expected margin delta table.
- Alyssa: if you'd like, we can slot a 30-minute call Wed 9 AM PT to walk through wording.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0317
